 Home » Agencies » FSIS issues alert for meat products tied to Listeria recall FSIS issues alert for meat products tied to Listeria recall
 Source: US Department of Agriculture 
 Nov 16, 2026 
 By Rachael Oatman 
 Add as a preferred
source on Google WASHINGTON — The US Department of Agriculture’s Food Safety and Inspection Service (FSIS) issued a public health alert on Nov. 14 for ready-to-eat (RTE) meat products containing Food and Drug Administration (FDA)-regulated biscuits that may be contaminated with Listeria monocytogenes .
 The problem was discovered when a company notified FSIS it received FDA-regulated biscuits that had been recalled by C.H. Guenther & Son.
 The RTE meat products subject to the health alert bear the establishment number “EST. 51248.” Under the “Mmm! Meals Made in Minutes” brand, the biscuit and sausage gravy items were primarily used for stocking vending machines, according to FSIS. They were distributed across Arkansas, Louisiana, Mississippi, Oklahoma, Tennessee and Texas.
 As more information becomes available, FSIS will update the public health alert.
 Currently, there have been no confirmed reports of illness due to consumption of the product, FSIS said.
